assessment.summary: Bloomberg's Forbes-estimated $64.2B net worth (Feb 2020) far exceeds the $6–11.4B collective wealth of the bottom 38% of US households (~125.7M people) per the original Bruenig analysis and PolitiFact's independent replication, so the claim is supported.

evidence.finding: PolitiFact's independent replicator (Gross, U. Michigan) found the bottom 38% of households hold about $6B (vs Bruenig's $11.4B), verifying Bloomberg owns more wealth than the bottom 38% of American households combined.
The original Feb 19, 2020 analysis: Bloomberg's $64.2B Forbes net worth vs $11.4B for the bottom 38% of households (~47.8M households × 2.63 members ≈ 125.7M people), nearly 6x greater.
Forbes estimated Bloomberg's net worth at $64.2 billion as of Feb 19, 2020, the net-worth figure underlying the comparison.

The wealth-distribution side relies on the Federal Reserve's triennial SCF; the 2016 wave (published Sept 2017) was the latest available at the runtime date, a standard but real data-vintage mismatch with the Feb 2020 Forbes estimate.

assertions.assertion: Former mayor of New York, US, Mike Bloomberg owns more wealth than the bottom 125 million Americans.

gaps: PolitiFact's verification was published 2020-03-02, after the 2020-02-19 runtime date, though it uses data contemporaneous with the debate.
Distribution data is from the 2016 SCF (latest then available); no 2019/2020 distribution data existed at runtime, mixing vintages with a Feb 2020 Forbes estimate.
The 'bottom 125 million' is an approximation from a 2.63-members-per-household conversion (~125.7M people).
Bloomberg's net worth traces to a single underlying source (Forbes); one retrieved Forbes profile snapshot reads $53B vs the $64.2B used, but either figure dwarfs the bottom 38%'s collective wealth.
next_queries: Retrieve the September 2020 SCF 2016-2019 report tables to check whether the bottom ~38% of households' collective net worth changed materially from 2016 levels.
Find contemporaneous critiques of the bottom-125-million comparison (e.g., negative-net-worth caveats) from outlets outside the progressive ecosystem.
Retrieve Forbes's Bloomberg profile history around February 2020 to reconcile the $53B and $64.2B snapshots.
